result:
result: not ready to merge. The three findings are closed and verify passes, but the repair has two defects, both from the `<!--` / `-->` rule.

changed: none (read-only).

checks: `bunx --no-install mise run verify` -> exit 0. Type-check, lint and format are clean; 2106 tests pass, 0 fail.

blockers:
1. **False refusal in the shared check.** `HTML_COMMENT = /<!--|-->/` in `/home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-launcher/packages/runtime/src/cli/workflow-check.ts` tests the raw source, so the Claude `Workflow` hook now refuses scripts it allowed before.
   - A classic script reads `<!--` and `-->` as comments only in code, never inside a string, template or regex.
   - I ran these through `workflowRefusal`. `log(\`a --> b\`)`, `agent('Map A --> B', …)`, and `a<!--a` are refused. `a < b` and `b < !b` pass.
   - The new test even asserts that `-->` in a template is refused.
   - Prompt text such as "A --> B" or "<!-- … -->" is plausible in a root-written workflow.
   - Fix: check only code tokens, for example with acorn's `onToken` or `onComment`, or by scanning the AST for adjacent `<`, `!`, `--` tokens. Keep a script-wide refusal only for what is actually unsafe.
2. **`docs/hooks.md` does not match the code.** The new "Script-mode differences" bullet says `-->` is refused "at the start of a line". The code refuses `-->` anywhere (`docs/pi/extensions.md` says "anywhere"). If fix 1 is applied, update both docs to match.

notes (optional):
- The `-->` test is named "at the start of a line" but uses `/* a */ -->`, which is not at line start; the anywhere-rule passes it regardless.
- The inline-input allowlist (`script`, `args`) also refuses `title` and `description`, which the package accepts and ignores, and `resumeFromRunId`. This is safe but may surprise a model.
- The `/code-review` findings (`extension.ts` session handlers awaiting the collection, catalog empty listing, 10s deadline plus grace, `${HOLYAGENT_PI_ROOT}` hint, `config` reserved in `pi-entry.ts`) are all outside the repair range and already on the base. I classify them optional and did not trace them further.

Closed as intended:
- The `<!--` bypass is refused.
- Block-level function declarations are refused; top-level and function-body declarations pass.
- The `export const meta =` rule mirrors the package's regex (`meta.ts:61`) and refuses a second line or a vetted export that is not first on its line.
- The `script`-plus-`name` case is closed by the allowlist.
- A project config with `pi.enable` false no longer lifts the gates. The user-only read passes no project folders, and an unreadable config fails closed.

I only read the Pi paths and did not run Pi or a live model.
